title: Composable pair with acyclicity; the couple of a double complex
statement:
Let $\mathcal A\xrightarrow{\,F\,}\mathcal B\xrightarrow{\,G\,}\mathcal C$
be additive functors, where $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ are Grothendieck
abelian categories (so they have enough injectives and the right derived
functors $R^nF$, $R^nG$, $R^n(G\circ F)$ are computed on injective
resolutions) and $\mathcal C$ is
abelian. An object $B\in\mathcal B$ is *$G$-acyclic* if $R^qG(B)=0$ for
$q>0$, and $(F,G)$ is a *composable pair with acyclicity* if $F(I)$
is $G$-acyclic for every injective $I\in\mathcal A$.

Let $E$ be a first-quadrant cohomological spectral sequence in
$\mathcal C$ starting at $E_2$, and put
$E_\infty^{p,q}:=E_{p+q+2}^{p,q}$ (from this page on the differentials
into and out of $(p,q)$ vanish). An *abutment* of $E$ to a family of
objects $(H^n)_{n\geq0}$ of $\mathcal C$ is a decreasing filtration of
each $H^n$ by subobjects

$$
H^n=F^0H^n\supseteq F^1H^n\supseteq\cdots\supseteq F^{n+1}H^n=0
$$

such that $F^pH^n/F^{p+1}H^n\cong E_\infty^{p,q}$ whenever $p+q=n$.

For a first-quadrant double complex $D^{\bullet,\bullet}$ in $\mathcal C$,
let $\operatorname{Tot}(D)$ be its total complex. Filtering
$\operatorname{Tot}(D)$ by either degree gives a bigraded exact couple,
and its derived couples give the two spectral sequences of $D$. The image
filtration
$F^pH^n=\operatorname{im}\bigl(H^n(F^p\operatorname{Tot}D)\to
H^n(\operatorname{Tot}D)\bigr)$ is an abutment of each of the two spectral
sequences of $D$ to $H^\bullet(\operatorname{Tot}D)$; in the first quadrant
it is finite in each degree, so convergence is automatic.

proof.text: The first paragraph defines the acyclicity predicate, rather than asserting a Grothendieck spectral sequence for arbitrary additive functors. By [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives], both source categories have enough injectives. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] to $F$, $G$, and $G\circ F$: the sources have enough injectives and the targets are abelian. One obtains a resolution by embedding $X$ into an injective, then successively embedding each cokernel into an injective; the differentials are the quotient maps followed by these embeddings, so their kernels are the preceding images. With an injective resolution $X\to I^\bullet$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], define $R^nv(X)=H^n(v(I^\bullet))$. The cited derived-functor computation and uniqueness make this independent of the resolution. Thus $R^qG(B)=0$ for $q>0$ and its universal quantification over $F(I)$ are well-defined predicates. No identification $R^0v=v$ and no left exactness is used.

proof.text: For a first-quadrant spectral sequence [def-sp-spectral-sequence], $d_r$ out of $(p,q)$ has target $(p+r,q-r+1)$ and the incoming map has source $(p-r,q+r-1)$. These are zero when $r>q+1$ and $r>p$, respectively. Both inequalities hold for every $r\ge p+q+2$. The successor-page homology isomorphisms therefore identify all these entries with $E_{p+q+2}^{p,q}$. Defining an abutment to be the stated finite decreasing filtration [def-sp-filtration] with the displayed graded-piece isomorphisms now involves only subobjects, quotients and these stable entries.

source.place: Tag 012K (section-filtered-complex), bidegree formula; Tag 012U (definition-filtered-complex-ss-converges); blueprint det-def-groth-ss, second paragraph

proof.text: Put $K=\operatorname{Tot}(D)$ and let $F$ be either degree filtration of [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Only $0\le i\le n$ contributes to $K^n$, so only finite biproducts are needed in $\mathcal C$. The two components of the total differential preserve or raise each filtered index, hence $F^pK$ is a subcomplex. In each degree the summands with filtered index exactly $p$ complement those with index $>p$. Consequently inclusion and projection give the degreewise split short exact sequence $0\to F^{p+1}K\to F^pK\to\operatorname{gr}^p_FK\to0$. This applies to each filtration separately, without identifying the two filtrations on cohomology.

source.place: Tag 012X (section-double-complex), the two displayed filtrations; Tag 012M (lemma-spectral-sequence-filtered-complex)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] to each short exact sequence in Step 3. Set $A^{p,q}=H^{p+q}(F^pK)$ and $T^{p,q}=H^{p+q}(\operatorname{gr}^p_FK)$. Inclusion, quotient and boundary give $a:A^{p,q}\to A^{p-1,q+1}$, $g:A^{p,q}\to T^{p,q}$ and $f:T^{p,q}\to A^{p+1,q}$. Exactness of the long sequence at these three positions says exactly $\ker a=\operatorname{im}f$, $\ker f=\operatorname{im}g$ and $\ker g=\operatorname{im}a$, with the indices supplied by the displayed arrows. Thus these are bigraded exact couples. Concretely, to use the convention of [def-sp-exact-couple], reindex both terms by $(P,Q)=(2p+q,-p)$, with inverse $(p,q)=(-Q,P+2Q)$. Then the bidegrees of $a,f,g$ are $(-1,1),(2,-1),(0,0)$, exactly that definition.

Use [lem-sp-derived-couple-exact] on either reindexed couple. Its derived couple exists and is exact; iterating gives $T_1=T$, $T_{r+1}=H(T_r,d_r)$. Indeed after $s$ derivations the differential in $(P,Q)$ has bidegree $(s+2,-s-1)$; the inverse change of coordinates gives $(s+1,-s)$ in $(p,q)$, so this is $d_{s+1}$. This is the filtered-complex spectral sequence: its initial term is $H^{p+q}(\operatorname{gr}^p_FK)$ and its maps are precisely the inclusion, quotient and connecting maps used in the filtered-complex exact-couple construction. Taking the first and second degree filtrations gives, by this construction, the two spectral sequences of $D$ in [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences]. They are first quadrant, since the graded complex at filtration index $p$ is zero for $p<0$ and has no terms in total degree below $p$; taking page cohomology preserves this zero region. Discard page one to obtain sequences starting at page two as in the definition.

For each of the two filtrations, [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences] gives the specific image filtration $F^pH^n=\operatorname{im}(H^n(F^pK)\to H^n(K))$ and the isomorphisms $E_\infty^{p,q}\cong F^pH^{p+q}/F^{p+1}H^{p+q}$. These are the spectral sequences of Step 5 because the theorem uses these same degree filtrations. Its stabilized terms identify with the page selected in Step 2, since $p+q+2>\max(p,q+1)$. To check the endpoints directly, $F^0K=K$ makes the first cohomology map the identity, while $F^{n+1}K^n=0$ makes $H^n(F^{n+1}K)=0$. Factorization through filtration inclusions makes the images decreasing. Hence $H^n=F^0H^n\supseteq\cdots\supseteq F^{n+1}H^n=0$, and the graded-piece isomorphisms exhibit the required abutment for each sequence. The two choices of $F$ may give different subobjects of $H^n(K)$.
